_doc: Human-facing facts about each router alias: real checkpoint, parameter count, and where to read more. Kept OUT of ai-router.yaml because LiteLLM does not pass custom model_info keys through /model/info (verified) — it returns only its own standard fields. Keyed by the alias in ai-router.yaml. Every field is optional; the UI degrades gracefully. Params for local models are exact counts from the Hugging Face repo; cloud vendors do not publish parameter counts, so those are intentionally absent rather than guessed.
_footprint_doc: `footprint` answers the only question that matters on a single 32 GB card: what does this model COST to have running, and what else can sit beside it. vramGb/ramGb are approximate by nature, so every entry carries a `basis` saying where the number came from — measured, or read off the launch flags. Do not add a footprint you cannot source in `basis`. Two different meanings are deliberately not averaged: vLLM RESERVES its share up front (the number is a floor you pay the moment it starts), while Qwen-Image PEAKS transiently and idles near zero because its weights live in host RAM. `service` is the BeTenshi service id, duplicated here so footprints still render when the router is down — the surface that most needs them. Cloud models have no footprint: they run off-box and cost money, not memory. Card total is 31.8 GB (32607 MiB).

local-qwen-image.note: Newer sibling available: Qwen/Qwen-Image-2512 (Dec 2025), same 20.4B size.

footprint.basis: VRAM measured: 20.3 GB peak mid-generation, ~0.1 GB idle. It does NOT hold the card — enable_model_cpu_offload() keeps the ~28 GB of fp8 weights in host RAM and streams them per stage. Note idleRamGb == ramGb and that is the point: the VRAM cost is transient but the HOST RAM cost is permanent for as long as the service is loaded (measured 21.7 GB resident while generating, 2026-08-01). That standing 28 GB is what collides with a FLUX run on a 63 GB box.

local-flux-schnell.note: Served through ComfyUI (:8188), not a router alias — the console builds the graph itself. Fast-draft tier beside Qwen-Image.

footprint.basis: VRAM measured 2026-07-30: card went to 31.72 GiB of 31.84 GiB during a 512x512 4-step run (35s cold). Weights on disk total 31.81 GiB — flux1-schnell 22.15, t5xxl_fp16 9.12, clip_l 0.23, ae 0.31 — so it effectively fills the card and nothing meaningful fits beside it. ComfyUI streams via cudaMallocAsync + comfy-aimdo DynamicVRAM, so torch_vram_total reads ~0.44 GiB and per-process attribution is NOT available: this figure is whole-card usage minus the 0.1 GiB Qwen-Image held idle at the time. IDLE measured 2026-08-01 with the service running but no workflow executed: torch_vram_total 64 MB, process resident 0.13 GB — ComfyUI loads checkpoints lazily on first execution and evicts after, so STARTING it costs nothing. ramGb is the host-RAM cost of an actual run, estimated from the weight total; that is what collides with Qwen-Image's standing 28 GB.

local-gemma4.note: Multimodal (text + image), 256K context, Apache-2.0. QAT weights rather than post-training AWQ: Google quantisation-aware-trains these, so the int4 build loses less than a naive 4-bit cast. Served by Ollama because the vLLM image here is 0.17.1 and has no gemma4 architecture (needs >= 0.19).

footprint.basis: Measured on this box 2026-09-14 during the Arabic experiment, at num_ctx 16384 (scripts/experiment-arabic.mjs samples nvidia-smi every 500 ms). Whole-card figure, so it includes the ~1.1 GiB the desktop was already holding; it is an upper bound, not a model-only allocation. kind=peak, NOT reserved: unlike vLLM, Ollama loads a model on demand and evicts it after OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE (5m here), so the card is free between uses - which is exactly why idleVramGb is ~0. The catch is that the peak is large enough that NOTHING else substantial fits while a model is resident, and OLLAMA_MAX_LOADED_MODELS=1 makes that explicit.

local-qwen3-vl.note: Multimodal, 256K context, Apache-2.0. Costs ~4 GiB more on the card than Gemma 4 31B for a comparable parameter count, because Q4_K_M is a post-training quantisation of a slightly larger model rather than a QAT build.
